title: Learning diaphragm breathing
summary: A bandmate teaches him diaphragm breathing; he practices constantly and within six months is leading the section.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: So after the first night, after I'd played with them, we rehearsed the show and everything. I was playing... Well, they only had one alto at the time, so I was playing the lead. They had two tenors. Stack(?) Walton played tenor and Lorenzo Lawson played the other tenor. And... I can give the full personnel of that band in a few minutes.

Anyway, so after the first night, at the end of the night, he took me back in the dressing room, he came and talked to me and he says, "Look, everything is going to be all right, but we've got to work on your power." And this was my first time hearing anything about diaphragm breathing on the saxophone. And he showed me how to do it. And I'll forever be grateful to him, because the air is still the most important thing when you're playing a wind instrument - - is how you use the air. And he showed me how to use this air and how to build my sound.
I worked hard. After I finished work every night, I practiced. Before I started work, I'd practice. I'd go home and practice late at night. I'd practice when I'd wake
up. But it paid off. Because six months later, I was kicking the platoons off! I was straw-bossing.
